io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.security.SecretStore

Packages that use SecretStore
Package
Description
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware
The board's own hardware and program-wide introspection: MCU and MCU hand out the board's pins, I2C bus, USB mouse, LED matrix, clock, BoardModel (which board the program was compiled for) and BoardMemory (Juno's arena and the program's flash usage).
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.internal
The board's native implementations: the classes whose methods are compiler intrinsics.
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.security
Secrets kept off the SD card and out of the firmware: SecretStore reads named values, and MCU.getSecretStore() selects the board's store — the Portenta H7's SE050C2, an ESP32 board's NVS, the Pico 2 W's TrustZone firmware or an AVR UNO's EEPROM.

    Modifier and Type
    Method
    Description
    static SecretStore
    MCU.getSecretStore()
    The selected board's store of named secrets, which is whatever that board actually has: the Portenta H7's NXP SE050C2, the ESP32-family boards' own non-volatile storage (also the UNO R4 WiFi's ESP32-S3 coprocessor's), the Pico 2 W's slots behind Juno's TrustZone secure firmware, or the AVR UNOs' on-chip EEPROM (UNO R3, UNO WiFi Rev2), the weakest of them.

    Modifier and Type
    Class
    Description
    final class 
    AvrEeprom
    Named-secret storage in the on-chip EEPROM of an AVR board: the UNO WiFi Rev2's ATmega4809 (256 bytes) and the UNO R3's ATmega328P (1 KB).
    final class 
    Esp32Nvs
    Named-secret storage in the non-volatile storage (NVS) of an ESP32, for the boards that carry no secure element at all: the ESP32-family boards' own chip, and the ESP32-S3 coprocessor of the UNO R4 WiFi, whose core's Preferences library has the same API and carries each call to the coprocessor over the modem link (it needs the coprocessor firmware 0.4.1 or later; an older one leaves the store unavailable).
    final class 
    Pico2WTrustZoneStore
    Named-secret storage on the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, kept by Juno's own TrustZone secure firmware: the RP2350 has no secure element, so a small program in the Cortex-M33's secure world holds the slots in a flash sector it fences off, and this program, which runs in the non-secure world, reaches them only through that firmware's one gateway.
    final class 
    Se050C2
    Named-secret storage in the NXP SE050C2 used by the Portenta H7.
